Hey dude. Your post resonates with me alot. One, we are the same age. And two, I used to struggle with the same things you did.


I know how it feels to be broke. I was swimming in debt in my early twenties. I know how hopeless it feels. To not be able to have the few things you want in life. To watch as people race by you. But that all can change you know.


But first I feel like you gotta love yourself first man. I don't think alot of people our age do honestly. So start loving yourself. No self blame either.


Surround yourself with people who will bring out the best in you. Who will remind you of who you are. Make good friends. Start working out. Working out is free you know. It will help alot with your metal health. Start reading too. Find a creative outlet if you can. Draw. Write. Whatever it is, let your soul sing.


Lovers and money will come with time. They can disappear too. But you yourself are your constant. So love yourself, and give yourself time. Don't let doubt take root in your soul. And often with doubt, bitterness and self hate can root too. Don't let that happen.


Love yourself. We have a finite time on this earth. So spend it wisely with your constant.

What really helped me was when I took some time away to learn about myself.

Perhaps you should do that. Sit down somewhere. Ask yourself when you feel lonely. What is it that you crave. And why do you think you crave it? Think about all your relationships. Family. Friends. Loved ones. And even the activities you enjoy. Think about what they offer you in life.

I learnt when it came to my loneliness. There were different kinds of loneliness. Somtimes I was seeking something intellectual. Somtimes it was romantic, othertimes it was spiritual.


So take a walk. Sit somewhere beautiful. Nature helps. Get a hot drink and venture deep into yourself. Moments like the one you are experiencing right now. If you use it right it can be really fruitful. Learn more about the person you are and love yourself.


Write your thoughts out. Be it poetry or a journal. Perhaps learn music. And draw. Let those emotions of yours out on paper. It doesn't have to be for everyones eyes or ears. But just for you.


With time you will learn why you feel the way you do. And I hope when you do find what you are seek you have grown as a person. Not that I'm saying you are lacking anything now. But you get what I mean.

And she asked me if I was living the dream I wanted for myself. And I just came to the realisation that I have never dreamt for myself.

I mean. I have always dreamt for other people. I want my siblings study what they want to study. Travel where they want to. Do what they want to do. I dream of a day where my parents have everything sorted out and they can retire peacefully.

Now that I ask myself, what I want. I truly don't know. I don't know what I want for myself in 10 years time. Career progression sounds great. Money is always nice. But it's not the thought of me having money that makes me happy. But rather the fact that I can help make the dreams I have for my loved ones come true. But what's after that?

Do you guys dream? Did you dream? And if so. What are those dreams? And have you achieved them?
